line: But me and my cubs, Wrigley (On bro, yeah, yeah)
vault_lines: But me and my cubs, Wrigley (On bro, yeah, yeah)
meaning:
Chief Keef hails from Chicago, Illinois, home to the Chicago Cubs, the professional baseball team that Sosa is referencing in this line. Keef refers to his closest friends as “cubs,” the mascot of the aforementioned MLB team, as well as name-drops their home stadium, Wrigley Field. It was constructed in 1914, and has been the beloved home of the Chicago Cubs for over a century.



Wrigley Field in Chicago, Illinois

The Chicago rapper is essentially implying that him and his associates are as tight-knit as the baseball team, especially when playing on their home turf of Wrigley Field.

There was even a fake flyer circulating in 2021 that proposed the idea of a Verzuz match between Chief Keef and fellow Chicago rapper, Lil Durk, with the speculative location being Chicago’s Wrigley stadium. Although, this was quickly confirmed to be illegitimate.

Cochise makes a reference to the WWE Hall of Famer RVD. RVD in his matches in ECW and WWE was known as a high flyer who jumped off the top rope a lot and springboarded off the ropes as well. His most well known move is the five star frog splash which he used as a finisher

line: Bro got the blicky (Blicky), got that boy doing the griddy (Yeah, yeah)
vault_lines: Bro got the blicky (Blicky), got that boy doing the griddy (Yeah, yeah)
meaning:
Cochise intimidates his opponent, inferring that whoever disrupts him will be struck by a “blicky” — another word for a pistol. He makes it clear that whoever his rival is will be so alarmed that they’ll begin running off and dancing — doing the Griddy.

Cochise previously asserted his intimidation with the blicky on his 2020 track with Internet Money, “Right Now”:

Had to keep the blicky on the hip (On the hip)

The Griddy is a dance trend that blew up in 2020 which most notably became a common touchdown celebration in the NFL. The dance involves tapping the ground with your heels and swinging your arms back and forth, which can be seen as an act of nervousness as Cochise implies.
